# Comparing two multi-base unit values, run on three backends.
#
# A unit value is a magnitude per base, so two of them are equal when every
# base agrees. Go compares its struct field-wise and Kotlin its data class
# component-wise, both for free; the interpreter compares its Amounts map; and
# JavaScript emitted `===` on two objects, which is reference identity and so
# was false for every pair the language calls equal. `sngl generate` exited 0
# on it and esbuild even warned -- "Comparison using the === operator here is
# always false" -- in a log nobody was reading.
#
# So this runs the comparisons rather than reading them. The html run is what
# makes the claim about JavaScript at all: a golden shows the emitted text, and
# only executing it shows that `a == b` for two equal measurements answers
# true. Before the fix that run reports four failures and the other two pass,
# which is the whole point of asking three backends the same question.
#
# `cancelled` is the case that separates two right-looking implementations: its
# em was added and subtracted away, so the interpreter's map holds no em key at
# all where the JS and Go records hold a zero. A base absent on one side and
# present-but-zero on the other has to compare equal, and a comparison written
# over "the bases this value carries" rather than over the unit's declared
# bases gets it wrong.
#
# The assertions are copied into bools by a mount effect because a test agent
# reads a component's own state rather than an expression over it.

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'


sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

component main ui.node {
    var a ui.measurement = 3px
    var b ui.measurement = 3px
    var wide ui.measurement = 3px + 2em
    var wider ui.measurement = 3px + 5em
    var cancelled ui.measurement = 3px + 2em - 2em

    var sameIsEqual = false
    var sameIsNotUnequal = true
    var oneBaseApartIsUnequal = false
    var oneBaseApartIsNotEqual = true
    var cancelledMatchesPlain = false
    var wideDiffersFromPlain = false

    effect(@mount {
        sameIsEqual = a == b
        sameIsNotUnequal = a != b
        oneBaseApartIsUnequal = wide != wider
        oneBaseApartIsNotEqual = wide == wider
        cancelledMatchesPlain = cancelled == a
        wideDiffersFromPlain = wide != a
    })

    ui.text(value="{sameIsEqual}")
}

// Two values written the same way are equal, and JavaScript said they were
// not: `===` asks whether the two records are the same object.
func testEqualValuesCompareEqual(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.sameIsEqual)
    t.assert(!c.sameIsNotUnequal)
}

// Differing in one base is unequal, which reference identity also answered --
// for the wrong reason, and so is no evidence on its own.
func testValuesDifferingInOneBaseCompareUnequal(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.oneBaseApartIsUnequal)
    t.assert(!c.oneBaseApartIsNotEqual)
}

// A base that cancelled to zero is the same value as one never written, so a
// record carrying a zero em equals one carrying no em at all.
func testACancelledBaseEqualsAnAbsentOne(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.cancelledMatchesPlain)
    t.assert(c.wideDiffersFromPlain)
}

ui.window {
    main
}
